title: External global-section tensor map is bijective
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, $g:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Assume $X,Y$ are quasi-compact and their diagonals over $k$ are affine. Let $F,G$ be quasi-coherent module sheaves [pqf-def-coherent]. The explicit $k$-linear map $T:S_f(F)\otimes_k S_g(G)\to S_{f\circ\operatorname{pr}_1}(\operatorname{pr}_1^*F\otimes\operatorname{pr}_2^*G)$ [def-sc-scalar-global-sections-comparison], induced by tensoring the projection pullback sections, is bijective. This is an assertion about ordinary sections, with no cohomology or cup comparison.

source.place: Tag 0BED, lemma-kunneth, equation-kunneth-on-cech; two finite-cover equalizers in degree zero

proof.text: Choose finite affine covers of X and Y. Affine diagonal makes their pairwise intersections affine. On each product of charts and each overlap, affine spectrum product, tensor-pullback sections and sheaf tensor sections identify T with the algebraic tensor section map. The unit and pure-tensor formulas make these maps restriction-compatible.

For a fixed affine V in Y, use the sheaf equalizer of the finite cover of X. Tensor over a field is exact and commutes with finite products, so this equalizer identifies sections on X times V with Gamma(X,F) tensor G(V). The comparisons commute with restriction in V.

Use the second finite sheaf equalizer on Y. Tensor with Gamma(X,F) again preserves its kernel and finite products. The resulting bijection equals T on pure tensors by the chart formulas, hence everywhere by tensor induction. Empty schemes and zero coefficients are included: the equalizers and their tensor products then have zero kernels.
